traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria from docs/stories/022.0-DEV-JSDOC-COEXISTENCE.story.md are satisfied with concrete implementation and passing tests:
- **Before/After/Mixed Positions of JSDoc Tags**: The valid-annotation-format rule’s tests exercise traceability annotations before, after, and interleaved with JSDoc tags (`@param`, `@returns`), all marked as requirements for this story and all passing. - **Proper Termination & Continuation Logic**: `processCommentLine` in `src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts` calls `isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine` and finalizes any pending `@story`/`@req` when a non-traceability JSDoc tag line is encountered, preventing further concatenation. Continuations are only applied when there is a pending annotation and the line is not a JSDoc tag. - **JSDoc Tag Boundary Detection**: `isNonTraceabilityJSDocTagLine` in `src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts` recognizes any line starting with `@` (other than `@story`, `@req`, `@supports`) as a JSDoc tag boundary, matching REQ-JSDOC-BOUNDARY-DETECTION. - **No False Positives & Multiline Preservation**: Tests such as `[REQ-NO-FALSE-POSITIVES] JSDoc tags do not pollute requirement ID when following @req` and `[REQ-PRESERVE-MULTILINE] multi-line @story annotation before other JSDoc tags` confirm that requirement IDs and story paths are parsed correctly without including following tags and that multiline values are preserved correctly. - **Backward Compatibility**: Existing tests for multiline parsing, configurable patterns, and @supports behavior (stories 005.0, 007.0, 010.1, 010.2) all continue to pass under the new logic, indicating no regressions. - **Documentation**: `docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md` includes a dedicated “JSDoc coexistence” section, explicitly referencing this story and describing the new behavior and example usage.
Given the targeted implementation changes, explicit traceability annotations, comprehensive tests tied to the 022.0 story, and a fully passing test suite, the story is fully implemented.
